messages.subject: se="bootstrap" changes test="Satorra.Bentler"
parts:
Hello,

I am a bit puzzled about the results from my CFA and I could not find anything in the documentation. I called the Satorra-Bentler correction with test = "Satorra.Bentler" to adjust the chi-square value and the fit indices. Additionally I called se = "robust" for robust standard errors for the parameter estimates. As robustness check, I also tried the combination test = "Satorra.Bentler, se = "bootstrap" and I expected to get the same Satorra-Bentler correction results, but different standard errors for the estimates. But it turned out, the adjusted chi-square value also changed and hence the fit indces, which I did not expect. So my question is, why did the se = "bootstrap" command innfluenced the test command? Are these fit indices also bootstrapped now or what happened here? 

As an example, I used the sample dataset from HolzingerSwineford1939. The  se = "bootstrap" does not change the ML statistics in all models, only the robust, adjusted values. 


Data <- HolzingerSwineford1939
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
set.seed(4143)
fit_SB <- sem(HS.model, Data, estimator = "ML", test = "Satorra.Bentler")
fit_BS <- sem(HS.model, Data, estimator = "ML", se = "bootstrap")
fit_SBBS <- sem(HS.model, Data, estimator = "ML", test = "Satorra.Bentler", se = "bootstrap")
summary(fit_SB,fit.measures=TRUE)
summary(fit_BS,fit.measures=TRUE)
summary(fit_SBBS,fit.measures=TRUE)

Many thanks for any suggestions.
Rainer

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: se="bootstrap" changes test="Satorra.Bentler"
parts:
The nature of the Satorra-Bentler correction is to adjust for the deviations of the variance-covariance matrix of the moment conditions/estimating equations from what would have been expected under the normal theory. I guess in this case, lavaan makes the call to use whatever non-MVNT matrix it has at hand... since the bootstrap produces a different covariance matrix than option "robust" does, the numbers are different.

The simulation work that I did when Ken Bollen and I worked on some Heywood papers convinced me that the "robust" option as is traditionally implemented in LISREL or MPlus underestimates the standard errors, as it fakes the "meat" of the sandwich estimate as a variance instead of MSE, and misses the misspecification biases. The true sandwich estimate (Stata's robust option) has its own underestimation problems, but at least they are supposed to go away asymptotically -- MPlus' "robust" option problems don't. (The propagation of inaccurate, overloading names for the methods is infuriating, but I was not the one inventing any of that.)
